sentences.en: In 2011, the body of a woman was discovered in a California vineyard.
sentences.zh: 2011年，人们在加利福尼亚州的一处葡萄园内发现了一具女性尸体。

sentences.en: She had been decapitated, and her body had been drained of blood.
sentences.zh: 她被斩首，且体内的血已被抽干。

sentences.en: It appeared her killer had gone to extraordinary lengths to conceal her identity.
sentences.zh: 看来她的凶手费尽了心思来隐瞒她的身份。

sentences.en: For more than a decade, she was known only as Jane Doe.
sentences.zh: 在十多年的时间里，她只被称为无名女尸。

sentences.en: Then, detectives finally learned her name, Ada.
sentences.zh: 随后，侦探们终于查出了她的名字——艾达。

sentences.en: But, identifying her only made this bizarre murder even more perplexing.
sentences.zh: 但是，确认她的身份反而让这起离奇的谋杀案变得更加扑朔迷离。

sentences.en: Ada is the new series from Casefile Presents, available now wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 《艾达》是 Casefile Presents 推出的全新系列节目，各大播客平台现已上线。

sentences.en: At 9.12am on Tuesday, September 11, 2001, 24-year-old Wells Crowther left a voicemail for his mother.
sentences.zh: 2001年9月11日星期二上午9点12分，24岁的韦尔斯·克劳瑟给母亲留了一条语音留言。

sentences.en: Speaking calmly, he said,
sentences.zh: 他语气平静地说：

sentences.en: Mum, this is Wells.
sentences.zh: 妈妈，我是韦尔斯。

sentences.en: I wanted you to know that I'm okay.
sentences.zh: 我想让你知道我很好。

sentences.en: Nine minutes earlier, a hijacked commercial aircraft had been deliberately flown into the South Tower of New York City's World Trade Center.
sentences.zh: 九分钟前，一架被劫持的商业客机被人蓄意撞向纽约世贸中心的南塔。

sentences.en: Marking the second major catastrophe that morning.
sentences.zh: 这也标志着那天早上的第二起重大灾难。

sentences.en: Seventeen minutes earlier, its neighbouring twin skyscraper, the North Tower, had been similarly hit.
sentences.zh: 十七分钟前，它毗邻的双子摩天大楼北塔也遭到了类似的撞击。

sentences.en: The 110-storey South Tower was struck between floors 77 and 85, several floors beneath the office where Wells Crowther worked as an equities trader.
sentences.zh: 这座110层高的南塔在第77层到第85层之间遭到撞击，正好位于韦尔斯·克劳瑟作为股票交易员工作的办公室下方几层。

sentences.en: After Wells phoned his mother to let her know he was alive, he raced down to the Sky Lobby on the 78th floor.
sentences.zh: 在韦尔斯给母亲打电话报平安后，他迅速冲到了78层的空中大堂。

sentences.en: The tip of the plane's wing had torn through the space, leaving burning carnage in its wake.
sentences.zh: 飞机机翼的尖端撕裂了这片空间，留下了一片燃烧的废墟。

sentences.en: A group of dazed and frightened survivors huddled at a bank of damaged elevators, nursing injuries ranging from burns and broken bones to cracked ribs and punctured lungs.
sentences.zh: 一群惊魂未定、满脸恐慌的幸存者挤在一排受损的电梯旁，他们身上带着各种伤痛，从烧伤、骨折到肋骨断裂和肺部穿孔不等。

sentences.en: Wells immediately took control of the chaotic situation and directed the survivors to an emergency stairwell that led to the ground level.
sentences.zh: 韦尔斯迅速控制了混乱的局面，并引导幸存者前往通往地面的紧急楼梯间。

sentences.en: Carrying one woman on his back, he guided the group down over a dozen floors before urging them to go on without him.
sentences.zh: 他背上背着一名女子，引导大家向下走了十多层楼，随后催促他们不用等他，继续前进。

sentences.en: He then headed back upstairs.
sentences.zh: 接着，他转身朝楼上走去。

sentences.en: By the time Wells made it back to the 78th floor, the area was overcome by thick, dark smoke.
sentences.zh: 等韦尔斯再次回到78层时，该区域已经被浓密的黑烟笼罩。

sentences.en: He stripped it down to his t-shirt, pulled a red bandana from his pocket and secured it over his nose and mouth so that he could breathe.
sentences.zh: 他脱得只剩下一件T恤，从口袋里掏出一条红头巾系在鼻子和口鼻上，以便能够呼吸。

sentences.en: Wells navigated through the debris until he came across more injured survivors.
sentences.zh: 韦尔斯在废墟中摸索前行，直到遇见了更多受伤的幸存者。

sentences.en: He retrieved extinguishers to put out the surrounding flames before administering first aid.
sentences.zh: 他找来灭火器扑灭周围的烈火，然后开始实施急救。

sentences.en: He then calmly announced,
sentences.zh: 接着，他平静地宣布：

sentences.en: Everyone who can stand, stand now.
sentences.zh: 所有能站起来的人，现在就站起来。

sentences.en: If you can help others, do so.
sentences.zh: 如果你能帮助别人，那就去做。

sentences.en: Wells led the group to the stairwell.
sentences.zh: 韦尔斯引导大家走向楼梯间。

sentences.en: As they rushed out onto the street, Wells remained in the tower to continue helping others.
sentences.zh: 当他们冲向街道时，韦尔斯留在了塔内，继续帮助其他人。

sentences.en: At 9.59am, 56 minutes after the plane's initial impact, the South Tower collapsed.
sentences.zh: 上午9点59分，即飞机首次撞击56分钟后，南塔倒塌了。

sentences.en: It was followed 29 minutes later by the North Tower.
sentences.zh: 29分钟后，北塔也随之倒塌。

sentences.en: In the aftermath of 9-11, stories from survivors surfaced about a mysterious man who had sacrificed his life to rescue them in the South Tower.
sentences.zh: 在9·11事件发生后，幸存者中流传着这样一个故事：有一位神秘男子在南塔中牺牲了自己的生命来营救他们。

sentences.en: They recalled the distinct red bandana he had worn across his face, which earned him the title, The Man in the Red Bandana.
sentences.zh: 他们回忆起他脸上系着的那条醒目的红头巾，这让他赢得了“红头巾男子”的称号。

sentences.en: When Alison Crowther read an article about the brave young man in the New York Times, she immediately knew who it was.
sentences.zh: 当艾莉森·克劳瑟在《纽约时报》上读到一篇关于这位勇敢年轻人的文章时，她一眼就认出了他是谁。

sentences.en: As a child, Wells Crowther watched his father Jeff get ready for church.
sentences.zh: 小时候，韦尔斯·克劳瑟看着父亲杰夫准备去教堂。

sentences.en: Jeff kept a comb handy, which he wrapped in a blue bandana tucked into his right hip pocket.
sentences.zh: 杰夫随身带着一把梳子，梳子包在一块蓝色头巾里，塞在右侧裤后袋里。

sentences.en: One day, Jeff gave his son his own bandana, in his preferred colour of red.
sentences.zh: 有一天，杰夫把自己的头巾送给了儿子，颜色是他最喜欢的红色。

sentences.en: It quickly became Wells' trademark.
sentences.zh: 这很快成为了韦尔斯的标志。

sentences.en: He wore it under his sports uniforms in high school and had it on him throughout his travels after graduation.
sentences.zh: 他在高中的运动服里面戴着它，毕业后旅行时也一直随身携带。

sentences.en: As he entered the corporate world, Wells kept his lucky bandana at his desk or in his back right pocket of his pants.
sentences.zh: 当他进入企业界工作时，韦尔斯把他的幸运头巾放在办公桌上或裤子的右后袋里。

sentences.en: When his colleagues asked why, Wells would reply,
sentences.zh: 当同事们问起原因时，韦尔斯总是回答：

sentences.en: With this red bandana, I'm going to change the world.
sentences.zh: 有了这条红头巾，我要去改变世界。

sentences.en: When shown photographs of Wells Crowther, the survivors confirmed he was the man who had saved them.
sentences.zh: 当看到韦尔斯·克劳瑟的照片时，幸存者们确认他就是那个救了他们的人。

sentences.en: Wells' remains were recovered six months in to the extensive clean-up of Ground Zero.
sentences.zh: 在对世贸中心遗址进行了长达六个月的大规模清理工作后，人们找到了韦尔斯的遗骸。

sentences.en: He was found alongside the bodies of firefighters and emergency services personnel who had been operating a command centre in the South Tower's ground lobby.
sentences.zh: 人们发现他的遗体与消防员及应急服务人员的遗体在一起，这些人员当时正在南塔地面大堂运营一个指挥中心。

sentences.en: It was believed that Wells had joined the other rescuers as they were preparing to free those trapped above before everything came crashing down.
sentences.zh: 人们相信，韦尔斯当时加入了其他救援人员的行列，正准备营救被困在上方的人，这时一切都坍塌了。

sentences.en: Courage, duty and care had been a major part of Wells' character throughout his life.
sentences.zh: 勇敢、责任感和关爱贯穿了韦尔斯的一生，成为他性格的重要组成部分。

sentences.en: While he loved working in the World Trade Centre, he hoped to one day get a job helping others directly.
sentences.zh: 虽然他热爱在世贸中心的工作，但他希望有一天能得到一份直接帮助别人的工作。

sentences.en: In the meantime, he was a fully trained volunteer firefighter and used those skills to save as many as 18 lives in the South Tower.
sentences.zh: 在此期间，他是一名受过全面培训的志愿消防员，并利用这些技能在南塔救下了多达18人的生命。

sentences.en: Speaking about Wells, one survivor said,
sentences.zh: 谈到韦尔斯时，一位幸存者说道：

sentences.en: People can live 100 years and not have the compassion, the wherewithal to do what he did.
sentences.zh: 人们可以活到100岁，却依然没有同情心，也没有能力去做他所做的事情。

sentences.en: Stories of Wells' actions on 9-11 helped his loved ones heal after the tragedy.
sentences.zh: 韦尔斯在9·11事件中的英勇事迹帮助他的亲人在悲剧发生后逐渐走出阴影。

sentences.en: They established the Wells Crowther Charity Trust, an organisation that awards young people who served their communities.
sentences.zh: 他们成立了“韦尔斯·克劳瑟慈善信托基金”，这是一个旨在表彰服务社区的年轻人的组织。

sentences.en: They hoped that Wells' story would inspire others to be more altruistic in their day-to-day lives.
sentences.zh: 他们希望韦尔斯的故事能激励其他人，在日常生活中更加无私。

sentences.en: His mother, Alison, said,
sentences.zh: 他的母亲艾莉森说：

sentences.en: We took a great peace in knowing that Wells, up until the end, was being very courageous, doing what he wanted to do.
sentences.zh: 我们感到极大的安慰，因为我们知道韦尔斯直到生命的最后一刻都非常勇敢，在做他想做的事。

sentences.en: He must have felt very fulfilled that day, knowing he was helping others.
sentences.zh: 那天他一定感到无比充实，因为他知道自己在帮助别人。

sentences.en: In the wake of 9-11, an organisation was founded called the World Trade Centre United Families Group, which aimed to help those affected by the attacks reconstruct their lives.
sentences.zh: 9·11事件发生后，成立了一个名为“世贸中心美国家庭联合会”的组织，旨在帮助受袭击影响的人们重建生活。

sentences.en: The group was primarily for the families of those who died in the tragedy, but survivors were also encouraged to join and seek support.
sentences.zh: 该组织主要面向在悲剧遇难者的家属，但也鼓励幸存者加入并寻求支持。

sentences.en: The group's online forum offered individuals a place where they could speak to fellow survivors who understood first-hand what they were going through.
sentences.zh: 该组织的在线论坛为个人提供了一个场所，让他们可以与切身经历过这一切的幸存者交流。

sentences.en: Inside their online community, survivors were met with empathy, understanding, and camaraderie as they bonded over their collective trauma.
sentences.zh: 在他们的网络社区内，幸存者们在共同的创伤中建立了紧密的联系，迎来了同理心、理解和袍泽之情。

sentences.en: They shared their harrowing stories and helped each other overcome immense feelings of grief, guilt, and regret.
sentences.zh: 他们分享了各自凄惨的故事，并互相帮助克服了巨大的悲痛、内疚和遗憾。

sentences.en: On Tuesday, May 13, 2003, 20 months after 9-11, a post was uploaded on the Survivors Forum by a new user.
sentences.zh: 2003年5月13日星期二，即9·11事件发生20个月后，一名新用户在幸存者论坛上发布了一则帖子。

sentences.en: It read,
sentences.zh: 上面写道：

sentences.en: I am only starting to feel the consequences now, despite having tried so hard to put it all behind me.
sentences.zh: 尽管我曾如此努力地想要把这一切抛在脑后，但现在我才刚刚开始感受到这些后果。

sentences.en: I don't sleep.
sentences.zh: 我睡不着觉。

sentences.en: I see and hear the images and sounds.
sentences.zh: 我的眼前总是浮现那些画面，耳边总是回响那些声音。

sentences.en: I'm moody.
sentences.zh: 我情绪反复无常。

sentences.en: My stress and anxiety have skyrocketed, and a variety of other things.
sentences.zh: 我的压力和焦虑急剧飙升，还有各种其他的问题。

sentences.en: For so long I pretended to be okay, that it is now hard to admit this is actually happening.
sentences.zh: 很长一段时间里，我都假装自己很好，以至于现在很难承认这一切正在发生。

sentences.en: I think I need to talk to someone about this and tell my story, but I don't see how I will manage that.
sentences.zh: 我想我需要找个人倾诉一下这件事情，讲述我的故事，但我不知道自己该怎么做到这一点。

sentences.en: Going through it once was more than enough.
sentences.zh: 经历一次就已经足够受的了。

sentences.en: The user signed their post off with their name, Tanya Head.
sentences.zh: 发帖人用她的名字坦娅·海德（Tanya Head）署了名。

sentences.en: Tanya's post elicited supportive comments from other survivors who welcomed her to the group and encouraged her to share her story.
sentences.zh: 坦娅的帖子引发了其他幸存者的支持性评论，他们对她加入该组织表示欢迎，并鼓励她分享自己的故事。

sentences.en: They explained that their forum was a safe, non-judgmental, and cathartic space to discuss all aspects of 9-11.
sentences.zh: 他们解释说，他们的论坛是一个安全、不带有偏见且具有宣泄作用的空间，可以讨论9·11事件的方方面面。

sentences.en: Tanya was praised for the courage it took for her to come forward.
sentences.zh: 坦娅站出来所需的勇气受到了大家的称赞。

sentences.en: The group awaited her opening up to them when she was ready.
sentences.zh: 大家都在等待她准备好向他们敞开心扉。

sentences.en: Tanya sporadically posted on the forum throughout May and June.
sentences.zh: 在5月和6月期间，坦娅偶尔会在论坛上发帖。

sentences.en: She was 28 years old and originally from Spain, but had immigrated to the US during her youth.
sentences.zh: 她今年28岁，原籍西班牙，但在年轻时移民到了美国。

sentences.en: By 2001, she was working for the distinguished investment management company Merrill Lynch in the World Trade Center's South Tower.
sentences.zh: 到2001年时，她在世贸中心南塔的杰出投资管理公司美林证券工作。

sentences.en: Like others, she was struggling immensely in the aftermath of the attack.
sentences.zh: 和其他人一样，她在袭击发生后也在艰难地挣扎。

sentences.en: While she maintained a happy disposition in real life, internally she was suffering.
sentences.zh: 虽然她在现实生活中保持着快乐的姿态，但内心里却备受折磨。

sentences.en: She rarely left her apartment, and whenever she closed her eyes, she was plagued by images of crashing planes, crumbling buildings, and mangled bodies.
sentences.zh: 她很少离开公寓，每当她闭上眼睛，脑海里就满是飞机坠毁、大楼坍塌和尸体残缺的画面。

sentences.en: Little things, like the sounds of planes overhead or the flicker of a candle flame, triggered frightening memories.
sentences.zh: 一些微小的事情，比如头顶飞过飞机的声音或烛光的闪烁，都会勾起她可怕的回忆。

sentences.en: Depression and panic attacks prevented Tanya from returning to work and had contributed to her gaining weight.
sentences.zh: 抑郁和恐慌症使坦娅无法重返工作岗位，并导致她体重增加。

sentences.en: While she was grateful for the support the other survivors showed her, she wasn't ready to share her full story just yet.
sentences.zh: 虽然她很感激其他幸存者对她的支持，但她还没准备好分享她完整的经历。

sentences.en: In June, members of the forum organised a visit to the remains of the Twin Towers.
sentences.zh: 6月，论坛成员组织了一次参观双子塔遗址的活动。

sentences.en: The area was cordoned off as clean-up efforts were still underway, but they intended to stand outside the barricade to reflect and grieve in each other's company.
sentences.zh: 由于清理工作仍在进行，该地区被拉起了警戒线，但他们打算站在警戒线外，在彼此的陪伴下进行反思和悼念。

sentences.en: Tanya had initially accepted the invitation, but on the night before it was due to take place, she phoned one of the organisers to cancel.
sentences.zh: 坦娅最初接受了邀请，但在活动前夕，她打电话给其中一位组织者取消了行程。

sentences.en: She said she was still fragile and wasn't ready.
sentences.zh: 她说自己依然很脆弱，还没有准备好。

sentences.en: For survivors of 9-11, the road to recovery was fraught with difficulties.
sentences.zh: 对于9·11幸存者来说，康复之路布满了艰难险阻。

sentences.en: Priority was given to those who died and the loved ones they'd left behind.
sentences.zh: 人们把优先权给予了死难者以及他们留下的亲人。

sentences.en: In contrast, survivors were regarded as the lucky ones and were expected to be grateful that they still had their lives.
sentences.zh: 相比之下，幸存者则被视为幸运儿，并被期望对能够保住性命心存感激。

sentences.en: Some felt their suffering was overlooked or misunderstood by the general public, media and government.
sentences.zh: 有些人觉得他们的痛苦被广大公众、媒体和政府所忽视或误解。

sentences.en: This feeling was amplified when an invite-only event was held at Ground Zero to mark the two-year anniversary of the attacks and some of the survivors were turned away.
sentences.zh: 当世贸中心遗址举办仅限受邀者参加的活动以纪念袭击两周年，而部分幸存者却被拒之门外时，这种感觉被进一步放大了。

sentences.en: In fact, none of the survivors had ever been permitted to access the site, unlike the families of those who had passed.
sentences.zh: 事实上，与遇难者家属不同，幸存者从未被允许进入该遗址。

sentences.en: Efforts to arrange a private tour were also denied, adding to ongoing feelings of invisibility for many survivors.
sentences.zh: 安排私人参观的努力也遭到了拒绝，这让许多幸存者挥之不去的不被重视感更加强烈。

sentences.en: Survivors vented their growing frustrations online, with a lot of their tensions directed towards the World Trade Centre United Families Group.
sentences.zh: 幸存者在网上宣泄着他们日益增长的不满，他们将许多情绪发泄在世贸中心美国家庭联合会身上。

sentences.en: One morning, Tanya Head logged into the forum and suggested the two groups split.
sentences.zh: 一天早晨，坦娅·海德登录了论坛，建议这两个组织分道扬镳。

sentences.en: They could create their own online support group, completely independent of the United Families.
sentences.zh: 他们可以创建自己的在线支持小组，完全独立于美国家庭联合会。

sentences.en: Tanya wrote, I think it's important that we stick together.
sentences.zh: 坦娅写道，我认为我们团结一致非常重要。

sentences.en: Other users agreed, and by that afternoon, they had established the World Trade Centre Survivors Forum.
sentences.zh: 其他用户表示赞同，到了那天下午，他们便成立了“世贸中心幸存者论坛”。

sentences.en: Within their new online space, users were able to open up like never before.
sentences.zh: 在他们的全新网络空间里，用户们能够前所未有地敞开心扉。

sentences.en: The switch appeared to liberate Tanya, who began posting more on this forum than she had the original.
sentences.zh: 这种转变似乎解放了坦娅，她在这个论坛上的发帖频率超过了最初的论坛。

sentences.en: Eventually, she felt comfortable to recount her personal story of survival.
sentences.zh: 最终，她感到可以舒适地讲述自己个人的生还故事了。

sentences.en: Tanya said she was chairing a meeting in a conference room on the 96th floor of the South Tower when the first plane hit the North Tower.
sentences.zh: 坦娅说，当第一架飞机撞击北塔时，她正在南塔第96层的一间会议室里主持会议。

sentences.en: Tanya and her colleagues flocked to the windows, where they observed the large smoking crater the aircraft had left in the neighbouring skyscraper.
sentences.zh: 坦娅和同事们涌向窗前，看到飞机在邻近的摩天大楼上撞出了一个冒烟的大洞。

sentences.en: Survivors of the impact emerged from the debris and clung to the crater's edge, waving and crying out for help as explosive flames inched closer behind them.
sentences.zh: 遭遇撞击的幸存者从废墟中钻出来，紧紧抓着大洞的边缘，挥手哭喊着求救，而身後逼近的熊熊烈火正步步紧逼。

sentences.en: Facing a terrible, fiery death, the survivors took matters into their own hands.
sentences.zh: 面对可怕的烈火死神，幸存者们决定自己掌握命运。

sentences.en: Some attempted to scale down the building to safety, while others jumped or fell to their deaths.
sentences.zh: 一些人试图顺着大楼爬到安全地带，而另一些人则跳楼或坠楼身亡。

sentences.en: It was a confronting and distressing sight that would haunt Tanya forever.
sentences.zh: 这是一个令人揪心且痛苦的景象，将永远缠绕在坦娅的梦魇中。

sentences.en: Tanya used her mobile phone to call her fiancé David, but the line was busy.
sentences.zh: 坦娅用手机给未婚夫大卫打电话，但线路占线。

sentences.en: A message was then relayed over the South Tower's public address system, urging occupants to stay put.
sentences.zh: 随后，南塔的公共广播系统传出一条消息，敦促大楼内的人员留在原地。

sentences.en: The collision at the North Tower was believed to be an isolated incident, and no one else was thought to be in any danger.
sentences.zh: 当时人们认为北塔的撞击只是一起孤立事件，其他人并没有处于任何危险之中。

sentences.en: Despite this reassuring message,
sentences.zh: 尽管有这番令人宽心的消息，

sentences.en: Tanya decided to leave.
sentences.zh: 坦娅还是决定离开。

sentences.en: She made her way to the bank of elevators in the sky lobby on the 78th floor, where an anxious crowd had already formed.
sentences.zh: 她来到了78层空中大堂的电梯旁，那里已经聚集了焦虑的人群。

sentences.en: Panic set in, and the crowd began pushing closer to the elevator doors.
sentences.zh: 恐慌情绪蔓延开来，人群开始向电梯门挤去。

sentences.en: Tanya recalled hearing one man yell,
sentences.zh: 坦娅回忆听到一名男子大喊：

sentences.en: Ladies, this is not the Titanic, it's not women and children firSt.
sentences.zh: 女士们，这不是泰坦尼克号，不是女士和儿童优先。

sentences.en: Then, a hysterical voice cried out,
sentences.zh: 接着，一个歇斯底里的声音尖叫起来：

sentences.en: There's another plane coming!
sentences.zh: 又有一架飞机飞过来了！

sentences.en: There's another plane coming!
sentences.zh: 又有一架飞机飞过来了！

sentences.en: The deafening roar of the approaching jet grew as it sped towards the South Tower.
sentences.zh: 随着逼近的喷气式飞机加速冲向南塔，震耳欲聋的轰鸣声越来越响。

sentences.en: Within seconds, the plane made contact and erupted into a powerful fireball.
sentences.zh: 几秒钟之内，飞机撞上了大楼，腾起了一个巨大的火球。

sentences.en: Its wing shattered through the walls and collapsed the ceiling.
sentences.zh: 它的机翼击碎了墙壁，并导致天花板坍塌。

sentences.en: Tanya felt a tremendous increase in pressure.
sentences.zh: 坦娅感到压力骤然剧增。

sentences.en: All the air in her lungs was sucked out, and for a moment, it seemed as though she was flying through the air.
sentences.zh: 她肺里的空气瞬间被抽干，有那么一瞬间，她觉得自己仿佛在空中飞翔。

sentences.en: Then, everything went black.
sentences.zh: 随后，一切都陷入了黑暗。

sentences.en: After recounting this experience to the World Trade Center Survivors Forum,
sentences.zh: 在世贸中心幸存者论坛上讲述了这段经历后，

sentences.en: Tanya stopped.
sentences.zh: 坦娅停了下来。

sentences.en: I find it very hard to talk about what happened afterward, she admitted.
sentences.zh: 她坦言，我发现很难谈论后来发生的事情。

sentences.en: The community rallied around Tanya until she felt comfortable to open up a little more.
sentences.zh: 社区成员纷纷围在坦娅身旁，直到她感到能够再多透露一些。

sentences.en: She recalled that after being knocked unconscious by the impact of the South Tower collision, she woke up under a broken slab of marble that had once been part of a wall.
sentences.zh: 她回忆说，在南塔撞击产生的冲击力将她震晕后，她在一块曾是墙壁一部分的碎大理石板下醒来。

sentences.en: Several fires illuminated the devastation around her.
sentences.zh: 几处火苗照亮了她身边的满目疮痍。

sentences.en: Lying alongside Tanya was a colleague who had been decapitated.
sentences.zh: 躺在坦娅身旁的是一位被斩首的同事。

sentences.en: Other mangled and charred bodies were scattered about, while the weary voices of survivors cried out in the darkness.
sentences.zh: 其他血肉模糊、烧焦的尸体散落各处，黑暗中传来幸存者疲惫的哭喊声。

sentences.en: Smoke burned Tanya's lungs, thick dust almost blinded her, and pain radiated through her body.
sentences.zh: 浓烟灼烧着坦娅的肺，厚重的灰尘几乎让她失明，剧痛传遍了她的全身。

sentences.en: She agonised over the realisation that this moment was going to be her laSt.
sentences.zh: 她痛苦地意识到，这一刻将是她的最后时刻。

sentences.en: Just as Tanya accepted her fate, someone began hitting her on the back.
sentences.zh: 就在坦娅接受了自己的命运时，有人开始拍打她的后背。

sentences.en: Each thud brought her immense pain.
sentences.zh: 每一次拍打都带给她巨大的痛苦。

sentences.en: She begged the person to stop, only to realise that her clothes were on fire and a man was using a jacket to pad out the flames.
sentences.zh: 她恳求那个人停下来，却发现自己的衣服着火了，一个男人正用夹克扑灭火焰。

sentences.en: A red bandana covered the lower half of his face, but Tanya could see his brown eyes were kind.
sentences.zh: 一条红头巾遮住了他脸部的下半部分，但坦娅能看出他的棕色眼睛很慈祥。

sentences.en: Just stay awake, he told her.
sentences.zh: 只要保持清醒，他对她说。

sentences.en: The man said he was going to show Tanya the way out.
sentences.zh: 那名男子说他会带坦娅找到出去的路。

sentences.en: Reassured by his calm presence,
sentences.zh: 在他平静的陪伴下，她感到了一丝安心，

sentences.en: Tanya mustered the strength to pull herself out from under the rubble.
sentences.zh: 坦娅鼓起力气，把自己从废墟下拉了出来。

sentences.en: That's when she noticed that her right arm was severely burnt and hanging from her body by a thread of sinew.
sentences.zh: 就在那时，她注意到自己的右臂严重烧伤，只剩下一根肌腱连在身上。

sentences.en: She tucked it into her jacket to keep it together.
sentences.zh: 她把它塞进夹克里固定住。

sentences.en: The man in the red bandana supported Tanya as they climbed and crawled through the wreckage.
sentences.zh: 头系红方巾的男子扶着坦娅，两人在废墟中艰难地攀爬和匍匐前进。

sentences.en: Each movement brought Tanya agonising pain and she doubted she could go on.
sentences.zh: 每一次挪动都给坦娅带来剧痛，她怀疑自己是否还能坚持下去。

sentences.en: Her rescuer encouraged her by saying,
sentences.zh: 她的救援者鼓励她说道：

sentences.en: Just keep moving.
sentences.zh: 继续走。

sentences.en: Along the way, the pair came across a badly burnt man gasping for air.
sentences.zh: 一路上，两人遇到了一名严重烧伤、大口喘气的男子。

sentences.en: Tanya knelt beside him and he handed her something small and hot.
sentences.zh: 坦娅跪在他身旁，他递给她一样小而温热的东西。

sentences.en: It was a gold wedding ring inscribed with a woman's name and the word forever.
sentences.zh: 那是一枚黄金结婚戒指，上面刻着一个女人的名字和“永远”这个词。

sentences.en: Please give this to my wife, he begged.
sentences.zh: 请把这个交给我的妻子，他恳求道。

sentences.en: I'll find her and I'll give it to her,
sentences.zh: 我会找到她，并把这个交给她，

sentences.en: Tanya replied.
sentences.zh: 坦娅回答说。

sentences.en: Just as she placed the ring into her pocket, the man took his final breath.
sentences.zh: 就在她把戒指放进口袋的那一刻，那名男子咽下了最后一口气。

sentences.en: Tanya proceeded onwards with the man in the red bandana.
sentences.zh: 坦娅和系红方巾的男子继续前行。

sentences.en: They eventually reached the door to an emergency stairwell where the man placed his hand on Tanya's shoulder and said,
sentences.zh: 他们最终到达了一处紧急楼梯间的门前，那名男子把手放在坦娅的肩膀上说：

sentences.en: Go, you can do this.
sentences.zh: 去吧，你能行的。

sentences.en: Tanya's mind raced with thoughts of her life, her family, her fiancé and their upcoming wedding.
sentences.zh: 坦娅的脑海中飞速闪过关于她的生活、她的家人、她的未婚夫以及他们即将举行的婚礼的种种思绪。

sentences.en: Compelled to power on, she began her descent.
sentences.zh: 在继续前进的信念驱使下，她开始向下走去。

sentences.en: The man helped her down each painful step until the smoke cleared and the rest of the way became clear.
sentences.zh: 那男子扶着她走过每一步痛苦的台阶，直到浓烟散去，前方的路变得清晰起来。

sentences.en: He removed his bandana, looked at Tanya resolutely and reassured her that she would be safe.
sentences.zh: 他摘下方巾，坚定地看着坦娅，并安慰她说她会很安全。

sentences.en: Just keep going down, I have to go back up and help other people, he said, before heading back towards the wrecked sky lobby.
sentences.zh: 只管往下走，我得返回上面去帮助其他人，他在转头返回损毁的空中大堂之前说道。

sentences.en: Tanya hobbled down until the pain, exhaustion and blood loss became too much and she passed out.
sentences.zh: 坦娅一瘸一拐地往下走，直到疼痛、精疲力竭和失血过多让她无法承受，晕倒了过去。

sentences.en: She was soon stirred awake by a firefighter who told her,
sentences.zh: 不久，她被一名消防员唤醒，消防员对她说：

sentences.en: We're leaving here together.
sentences.zh: 我们一起离开这里。

sentences.en: He carried Tanya down the remaining 20 floors and out onto the street.
sentences.zh: 他背着坦娅走完了剩下的20层楼，来到了街上。

sentences.en: They had barely made it out when the ground began to shake.
sentences.zh: 他们才刚刚逃生，地面就开始剧烈震动起来。

sentences.en: The thunderous sound of crushing concrete and metal filled the air.
sentences.zh: 震耳欲聋的混凝土和金属碎裂声充斥着空气。

sentences.en: People all around began running away in panic.
sentences.zh: 周围的人们开始惊慌失措地四处逃窜。

sentences.en: Tanya was thrust under a fire truck just as the South Tower collapsed behind her.
sentences.zh: 就在南塔在她身后倒塌的那一刻，坦娅被推到了一辆消防车底下。

sentences.en: Her next memory was waking in hospital five days later.
sentences.zh: 她醒来后的下一个记忆是五天后在医院里。

sentences.en: Her arm had been reattached but she would only ever have partial use of it and the burn scars would remain.
sentences.zh: 她的手臂已经接上，但永远只能恢复部分功能，烧伤的疤痕也将伴随一生。

sentences.en: Tanya's distraught parents were by her side.
sentences.zh: 坦娅心急如焚的父母守在她的床边。

sentences.en: Where's Dave?
sentences.zh: 戴夫在哪？

sentences.en: she asked.
sentences.zh: 她问。

sentences.en: Tanya's fiancé David worked for a consulting firm on the 100th floor of the North Tower.
sentences.zh: 坦娅的未婚夫戴维在北塔100层的一家咨询公司工作。

sentences.en: She would come to learn that he didn't make it.
sentences.zh: 后来她才知道，他没能逃出来。

sentences.en: Case File will be back shortly.
sentences.zh: 《案件档案》稍后将继续播出。

sentences.en: Thank you for supporting us by listening to this episode's sponsors.
sentences.zh: 感谢您通过收听本期节目的赞助商来支持我们。

sentences.en: Thank you for listening to this episode's ads.
sentences.zh: 感谢您收听本期节目的广告。

sentences.en: By supporting our sponsors you support Case File to continue to deliver quality content.
sentences.zh: 通过支持我们的赞助商，您就是在支持《案件档案》继续为您提供优质内容。

sentences.en: Tanya Head's survival was nothing short of incredible.
sentences.zh: 坦娅·海德的生还简直是个奇迹。

sentences.en: In the North Tower the plane had hit between floors 93 and 98 in a manner that decimated all forms of escape.
sentences.zh: 在北塔，飞机撞击了第93层到第98层之间，彻底摧毁了所有的逃生通道。

sentences.en: At the crash site and above over 1,300 people died.
sentences.zh: 在撞击点及上方，有1300多人丧生。

sentences.en: There were no survivors.
sentences.zh: 无人生还。

sentences.en: It might have been a similar outcome in the South Tower had it not been for two special circumstances.
sentences.zh: 如果不是因为两个特殊情况，南塔的结局可能也会如此。

sentences.en: Firstly the emergency stairwell was far enough from the impact zone to remain usable.
sentences.zh: 首先，紧急楼梯间距离撞击区足够远，因而还能使用。

sentences.en: Secondly the man in the red bandana
sentences.zh: 其次，那位系红方巾的男子

sentences.en: Wells Crowther.
sentences.zh: 韦尔斯·克劳瑟。

sentences.en: Survivor Ling Young described Wells as their guardian angel saying without him we would be sitting there waiting until the building came down.
sentences.zh: 幸存者凌·扬将韦尔斯描述为他们的守护天使，并说如果没有他，我们就会坐在那里等着大楼倒塌。

sentences.en: Tanya Head was one of the lucky few saved by Wells that day.
sentences.zh: 坦娅·海德是那天被韦尔斯救出的少数幸运儿之一。

sentences.en: But the loss of her fiancé in the North Tower made her experience uniquely devastating.
sentences.zh: 但未婚夫在北塔的不幸遇难，让她的经历变得异常残酷和打击巨大。

sentences.en: She was the only person to be both a tower survivor of the 9-11 attack and a bereaved family member of a life it claimed.
sentences.zh: 她是唯一一个既是9·11袭击中大楼的幸存者，又是遇难者家属的人。

sentences.en: Tanya's extraordinary story soon caught the attention of Jerry Bogaz a planning director for the New York
sentences.zh: 坦娅不寻常的故事很快引起了纽约大都会交通委员会规划总监杰里·博加斯的注意

sentences.en: Metropolitan Transportation Council.
sentences.zh: 大都会交通委员会。

sentences.en: Jerry had fled from the North Tower before it collapsed but several members of his team had stayed behind and died.
sentences.zh: 杰里在北塔倒塌前逃了出去，但他的团队中有几名成员留在了大楼里并丧生了。

sentences.en: In the devastating aftermath
sentences.zh: 在毁灭性的灾难发生之后，

sentences.en: Jerry spearheaded several in-person survivors' meetings throughout the city as a means of support.
sentences.zh: 杰里在全市发起并主持了几场幸存者见面会，以此作为一种支持的方式。

sentences.en: It was through these that he learned about Tanya Head and was in awe of her story.
sentences.zh: 正是在这些活动中，他了解到了坦娅·海德的事迹，并对她的故事惊叹不已。

sentences.en: He reached out to Tanya online and the two bonded over their shared ordeal.
sentences.zh: 他在网上联系了坦娅，两人因共同的劫后余生经历而结下了深厚的羁绊。

sentences.en: Like Jerry
sentences.zh: 就像杰里一样，

sentences.en: Tanya was using her struggles as motivation to help others.
sentences.zh: 坦娅将自己的挣扎转化为帮助他人的动力。

sentences.en: She said it gave her the will to live.
sentences.zh: 她说这给了她活下去的意志。

sentences.en: Jerry was struck by Tanya's optimism and resilience despite all she had loSt.
sentences.zh: 尽管失去了那么多，坦娅的乐观和韧劲还是深深打动了杰里。

sentences.en: He invited her to attend one of his meetings set for Saturday
sentences.zh: 他邀请她参加定于2004年1月24日星期六举行的其中一场见面会，她欣然接受了。

sentences.en: January 24, 2004 and she willingly accepted.
sentences.zh: 2004年1月24日，她欣然接受了。

sentences.en: While no one in any of the survivor circles had met Tanya in real life yet everyone knew her story and she'd become somewhat of a celebrity among them.
sentences.zh: 虽然幸存者圈子里没有人真正在现实中见过坦娅，但所有人都知道她的故事，她在他们当中成了一种名人。

sentences.en: But Tanya didn't relish the attention.
sentences.zh: 但坦娅并不留恋这种关注。

sentences.en: When she attended
sentences.zh: 当她参加

sentences.en: Jerry Bogaz's meeting the other guests found her to be unassuming and shy.
sentences.zh: 杰里·博加斯的见面会时，其他来宾发现她谦逊而害羞。

sentences.en: While she was responsive and grateful for their support she was happy to sit quietly as the meeting took place around her.
sentences.zh: 虽然她对他们的支持做出回应并心存感激，但当会议在她身边进行时，她很乐意安静地坐着。

sentences.en: Jerry Bogaz spoke of his vision to create a non-profit organisation specifically for 9-11 survivors that would help empower individuals to find renewed purpose.
sentences.zh: 杰里·博加斯谈到了他建立一个专门针对9·11幸存者的非营利组织的设想，该组织将帮助赋能个人去寻找重新燃起的使命感。

sentences.en: The organisation intended to implement a day of recognition titled Survivor's Day and aimed to finally get survivors' access to Ground Zero.
sentences.zh: 该组织计划设立一个名为“幸存者日”的表彰日，并旨在最终让幸存者能够进入世贸中心遗址（Ground Zero）。

sentences.en: From there they hoped to provide input on a memorial for the site.
sentences.zh: 从那里开始，他们希望为该遗址的纪念碑建设提供意见。

sentences.en: The group settled on a name the World Trade Centre
sentences.zh: 该组织最终确定了一个名字：世界贸易中心

sentences.en: Survivors Network.
sentences.zh: 幸存者网络。

sentences.en: Tanya suggested that the network join forces with her online group the Survivors Forum.
sentences.zh: 坦娅建议该网络与她的网络群组“幸存者论坛”强强联手。

sentences.en: Not only would they have more political clout with greater numbers they could also share the arduous task of identifying and reaching out to the thousands of people
sentences.zh: 这样不仅能凭借更多的人数拥有更大的政治影响力，他们还可以分担那项艰巨的任务：寻找并联系数千名

sentences.en: who had survived
sentences.zh: 在9·11中生还的

sentences.en: 9-11 to offer their support.
sentences.zh: 人，向他们提供支持。

sentences.en: By the end of the meeting
sentences.zh: 到会议结束时，

sentences.en: Tanya had come out of her shell and was fiercely determined.
sentences.zh: 坦娅已经打破了内向的性格，变得无比坚定。

sentences.en: That night she sat at her computer contacting an array of people who could help the network and its members.
sentences.zh: 那天晚上，她坐在电脑前，联系了一批能够帮助该网络及其成员的人。

sentences.en: Six weeks later
sentences.zh: 六周后，

sentences.en: Tanya sent an email to the Survivors Network announcing good news.
sentences.zh: 坦娅向幸存者网络发送了一封电子邮件，宣布了一个好消息。

sentences.en: She had contacted the World Trade Centre site supervisor and after years of inexplicable rejection she had successfully negotiated a private visit to Ground Zero.
sentences.zh: 她联系了世贸中心遗址主管，在经历了多年莫名其妙的拒绝后，她成功协商到了一次私人访问世贸中心遗址的机会。

sentences.en: The group was elated.
sentences.zh: 大家欣喜若狂。

sentences.en: The tour took place on Friday
sentences.zh: 这次参观于2004年5月14日星期五举行

sentences.en: May 14
sentences.zh: 5月14日

sentences.en: 2004 with 20 survivors opting to take part.
sentences.zh: 有20名幸存者选择参加。

sentences.en: Unlike those around her this was not
sentences.zh: 与她周围的人不同，这并不是

sentences.en: Tanya's first visit to Ground Zero.
sentences.zh: 坦娅第一次访问世贸中心遗址。

sentences.en: Because her fiancé had died in the attacks she had gone on one of the first private tours held for family members of the deceased.
sentences.zh: 由于她的未婚夫在袭击中丧生，她曾参加过专为死者家属举办的首批私人参观活动之一。
